The authors build on a prior result showing that the NG action for D = 2+2 target space-time possesses a manifest global SL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR) symmetry, which they denote [SL(2, IR)]3. They argue that the GS formulation is more advantageous than the Neveu-Schwarz-Ramond (NSR) formulation for rewriting the action purely in terms of a determinant, because the GS formulation lacks explicit world-sheet supersymmetry. The central result is that, after eliminating the zweibein (2D metric) via its non-algebraic field equation, the NG part of the GS action becomes the square root of the Cayley's hyperdeterminant of the superspace pull-back, written as sqrt(Det(Πiα.α)). This object is manifestly invariant under [SL(2, IR)]3, acting on the three indices i, α, and .α carried by the pull-back. The authors also demonstrate that the action retains fermionic kappa-symmetry, which guarantees light-cone equivalence to the conventional N = 2 GS superstring and to the N = 2 NSR superstring at the classical level. They emphasize that the resulting action and its fermionic transformation rule involve neither the 2D metric gij, the zweibein ei(j), nor the factor Phi containing these fields, indicating total consistency purely in terms of the superspace coordinates ZM. The target superspace D = (2, 2; 2, 2) is highlighted as the natural background for self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SDSYM) multiplets, which are proposed as the underlying theory for all supersymmetric integrable systems in dimensions D <= 3. The paper explicitly refrains from claiming quantum-level equivalence, noting that even the NG-to-Polyakov equivalence is not well established at the quantum level. The work is a purely classical, analytical derivation with no numerical computations, datasets, or experimental components. The authors acknowledge W. Siegel and the referee for noticing mistakes in an earlier version. The paper contributes to the broader conjecture that self-dual Yang-Mills theory generates all bosonic integrable models in dimensions D <= 3, which is proposed to be supersymmetrized. The significance of the D = 2+2 signature is attributed to the isomorphism SO(2, 2) approx SL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR), which is contrasted with SO(3, 1) approx SL(2, C) for D = 3+1, which is deemed unsuitable for SL(2, IR). The paper also notes that in D = 2+2, unlike D = 3+1, the components α and .α are not related by complex conjugation. The authors justify the NG formulation with the 2D metric eliminated by analogy to how the sigma-model Kahler structure emerges only after auxiliary fields are eliminated in N = 1 local supersymmetry in 4D. Overall, the paper provides a rigorous classical demonstration that the global [SL(2, IR)]3 symmetry becomes manifest through the Cayley's hyperdeterminant structure, reinforcing the summary.title: Green-Schwarz, Nambu-Goto Actions, and Cayley's Hyperdeterminant
summary.field_subfield: Theoretical physics: superstring theory and integrable systems
summary.executive_summary: This paper establishes a classical-level equivalence between the Green-Schwarz (GS) sigma-model action for the N = 2 superstring and the Nambu-Goto (NG) action re-expressed through Cayley's hyperdeterminant, in a target superspace of dimension D = (2, 2; 2, 2). The authors build on a prior result showing that the NG action for D = 2+2 target space-time possesses a manifest global SL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR) symmetry, which they denote [SL(2, IR)]3. They argue that the GS formulation is more advantageous than the Neveu-Schwarz-Ramond (NSR) formulation for rewriting the action purely in terms of a determinant, because the GS formulation lacks explicit world-sheet supersymmetry. The central result is that, after eliminating the zweibein (2D metric) via its non-algebraic field equation, the NG part of the GS action becomes the square root of the Cayley's hyperdeterminant of the superspace pull-back, written as sqrt(Det(Πiα.α)). This object is manifestly invariant under [SL(2, IR)]3, acting on the three indices i, α, and .α carried by the pull-back. The authors also demonstrate that the action retains fermionic kappa-symmetry, which guarantees light-cone equivalence to the conventional N = 2 GS superstring and to the N = 2 NSR superstring at the classical level. They emphasize that the resulting action and its fermionic transformation rule involve neither the 2D metric gij, the zweibein ei(j), nor the factor Phi containing these fields, indicating total consistency purely in terms of the superspace coordinates ZM. The target superspace D = (2, 2; 2, 2) is highlighted as the natural background for self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SDSYM) multiplets, which are proposed as the underlying theory for all supersymmetric integrable systems in dimensions D <= 3. The paper explicitly refrains from claiming quantum-level equivalence, noting that even the NG-to-Polyakov equivalence is not well established at the quantum level. The work is a purely classical, analytical derivation with no numerical computations, datasets, or experimental components. The authors acknowledge W. Siegel and the referee for noticing mistakes in an earlier version. The paper contributes to the broader conjecture that self-dual Yang-Mills theory generates all bosonic integrable models in dimensions D <= 3, which is proposed to be supersymmetrized. The significance of the D = 2+2 signature is attributed to the isomorphism SO(2, 2) approx SL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR), which is contrasted with SO(3, 1) approx SL(2, C) for D = 3+1, which is deemed unsuitable for SL(2, IR). The paper also notes that in D = 2+2, unlike D = 3+1, the components α and .α are not related by complex conjugation. The authors justify the NG formulation with the 2D metric eliminated by analogy to how the sigma-model Kahler structure emerges only after auxiliary fields are eliminated in N = 1 local supersymmetry in 4D. Overall, the paper provides a rigorous classical demonstration that the global [SL(2, IR)]3 symmetry becomes manifest through the Cayley's hyperdeterminant structure, reinforcing the interconnectedness of Cayley's hyperdeterminant, N = 2 superstring theory, SDSYM theory, and supersymmetric integrable models.

Executive Summary
This paper establishes a classical-level equivalence between the Green-Schwarz (GS) sigma-model action for the N = 2 superstring and the Nambu-Goto (NG) action re-expressed through Cayley's hyperdeterminant, in a target superspace of dimension D = (2, 2; 2, 2). The authors build on a prior result showing that the NG action for D = 2+2 target space-time possesses a manifest global SL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR)xSL(2, IR) symmetry, which they denote [SL(2, IR)]3. They argue that the GS formulation is more advantageous than the Neveu-Schwarz-Ramond (NSR) formulation for rewriting the action purely in terms of a determinant, because the GS formulation lacks explicit world-sheet supersymmetry. The central result is that, after eliminating the zweibein (2D metric) via its non-algebraic field equation, the NG part of the GS action becomes the square root of the Cayley's hyperdeterminant of the superspace pull-back, written as sqrt(Det(Πiα.α)). This object is manifestly invariant under [SL(2, IR)]3, acting on the three indices i, α, and .α carried by the pull-back. The authors also demonstrate that the action retains fermionic kappa-symmetry, which guarantees light-cone equivalence to the conventional N = 2 GS superstring and to the N = 2 NSR superstring at the classical level. They emphasize that the resulting action and its fermionic transformation rule involve neither the 2D metric gij, the zweibein ei(j), nor the factor Phi containing these fields, indicating total consistency purely in terms of the superspace coordinates ZM. The target superspace D = (2, 2; 2, 2) is highlighted as the natural background for self-dual supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SDSYM) multiplets, which are proposed as the underlying theory for all supersymmetric integrable systems in dimensions D <= 3. The paper explicitly refrains from claiming quantum-level equivalence, noting that even the NG-to-Polyakov equivalence is not well established at the quantum level. The work is a purely classical, analytical derivation with no numerical computations, datasets, or experimental components. The authors acknowledge W. Siegel and the referee for noticing mistakes in an earlier version.
